note: Curated AEM Guides product vocabulary for acceptance criteria. Two lists: 'block' = phrases that name a product concept the product does NOT have (invented from support/ticket wording) - fail-closed when they appear in an AC line. 'advise' = correct-term nudges that are too broad to hard-fail (the wrong word can be legitimate elsewhere) - surfaced as advisory suggestions only. Patterns are case-insensitive regex over an AC line. Every block/advise entry is HUMAN_APPROVED; add those rules only from a real human correction with the source Jira. canonical_terms can also contain documented names with DOCUMENT_VERIFIED provenance in canonical_term_sources; that is not Human approval or an acceptance contract. This encodes product vocabulary, NOT a code-identifier list - never put method/class names here.

block.message: There is no 'stale preset' concept in AEM Guides. It is an existing preset; recreating it (delete + create again) was a support workaround, not a product mechanism. Do not assert stale-preset detection or advice - move any 'show the preset needs recreation' requirement to an Open Question.

advise.correct: in merged.html inside Retain temporary files
advise.message: For a Native PDF check of the retained merged.html artifact, write 'In merged.html inside Retain temporary files'. If inspecting a different artifact, name that actual file instead; do not rename all temporary HTML to merged.html. Retain temporary files is a setting, not a folder. This is terminology guidance only, not an extra acceptance requirement.
advise.source_context: Human terminology correction in the current Native PDF UAC review

advise.message: AEM Guides has no per-run 'workflow' object. Use 'output history' (a run's output history). ('workflow' alone is a real AEM concept - only the run-workflow collocation is wrong.)
It is the 'output history', not an 'output-history record/details'. Drop the trailing noun.

advise.correct: the generated output in the fmdita-outputs folder set for that preset
advise.message: 'generated file' is vague. Name the concrete location: the generated output lands in the fmdita-outputs folder set for that preset.
There is no 'conditional preview' or 'simple preview' surface. The preview surface is called Editor Preview.

advise.correct: Baseline Panel / Map Panel / Translation Panel / Conditions panel / Subject Scheme Panel
advise.message: The Baseline, Map, Translation, Conditions, and Subject Scheme surfaces are PANELS, not dashboards. Use 'Baseline Panel', 'Map Panel', 'Translation Panel', etc. 'dashboard' is only for publish/output surfaces (e.g. the Bulk Publish dashboard, the Map Dashboard Outputs tab).

advise.wrong: regional value / generic value / N-character locale
advise.correct: a language variable has a value per language (language code, e.g. pt vs pt_br); missing value falls back to the UI language
advise.message: Do not invent locale/value terminology. A language variable holds a value per LANGUAGE (language code such as pt or pt_br); when a value is not defined for the output language it falls back to the UI language (per the language-variables doc - query RAG). Use concrete language codes (pt, hi, pt_br), not 'regional value / generic value / N-character locale'.

advise.wrong: Rule Editor / Visual Rule Editor / Advanced Map Editor / Theme Editor
advise.correct: Editor (with Author View, Source View, Preview) / Map console / Theme Page
advise.message: These are not AEM Guides concepts (platform terms that leaked into the corpus). The Guides authoring surface is the Editor with Author View, Source View, and Preview. 'Advanced Map Editor' is the Map console; 'Theme Editor' should be Theme Page. There is no Rule Editor / Visual Rule Editor in Guides.

advise.correct: Schematron Panel / Schematron File / Content Health report
advise.message: There is no 'Schematron Validation Report'. The real terms are the Schematron Panel and the Schematron File; Schematron can be used in the Content Health report.

advise.wrong: moved to the wrong group / move to a group
advise.correct: conditions are grouped automatically by their attribute; there is no move operation
advise.message: There is no 'move to a group' operation for conditions in Guides (grouping is automatic by attribute). Do not use invented operation verbs in ACs - verify every action verb is a real Guides operation, including in negative/boundary ACs.
